title: Counting Tilings

constraints.text: n ≤ 10 rows, m ≤ 1000 columns, 1×2 and 2×1 tiles

explanation: One side is ≤ 10: sweep the long side and keep a bitmask of which cells in the current column are already covered by tiles sticking out from the previous column.
traps: 2^10 masks × 2^10 transitions per column × 1000 is ~1e9 if done naively; generate transitions by DFS over the column (or go cell by cell).

extraLayers.prompt: What should the DP state represent?

options.text: dp[col][mask] = ways to fully cover columns < col, where mask marks cells of column col already covered by horizontal tiles
dp[i][j] = ways to tile an i × j rectangle
options.why: Sub-rectangles don't combine: tiles cross any cut you choose.

options.text: dp[col] = ways to tile the first col columns completely
options.why: Horizontal tiles stick out across the column boundary; you must remember which cells they cover.

extraLayers.explanation: Short side ≤ 10 → the 'frontier' between columns fits in a bitmask: that's profile DP.

extraLayers.prompt: Given that state, which transition is right?

options.text: From (col, mask): fill column col's free cells with vertical pairs or horizontal tiles starting here; the horizontal ones form next_mask; dp[col+1][next_mask] += dp[col][mask]

options.why: Tile choices depend on which cells are free.

options.text: dp[col+1][next] += dp[col][mask] for every pair of masks
options.why: Most pairs aren't compatible; you must check the column can be filled.

options.text: Raise the 2^n × 2^n transition matrix to the m-th power
options.why: Valid in principle but 1024³ per multiplication is far slower than the direct sweep for m ≤ 1000.

extraLayers.explanation: Answer = dp[m][0]: everything covered and nothing sticking out of the grid.
